title: Integrate new open models into catalog: metadata, pinning, and perf-profile docs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: onboard two newly vetted open-weight models (llama3-13b-open and falcon-40-lite-open) into the public model catalog with complete metadata records, explicit version-pinning support, and published performance profiles. Deliverables: 1) schema entries in the catalog service (name, canonical id, versions, compatible runtime flavors, quantization options, memory/throughput profile, recommended pinning string); 2) static performance profiles published to docs and surfaced in Console per-model page; 3) SDK/docs examples showing how to pin to a specific model version and how to select a cost/latency optimized variant; 4) changelog + migration notes for customers who relied on soft aliasing; 5) end-to-end validation in staging with automated regression tests for latency and output parity on a canonical prompt set. Out-of-scope: model weights ingestion and licensing review (completed separately).
acceptance_criteria: Catalog entries created and validated in staging with unique canonical IDs
Version pinning works via API and SDK examples (requests using model_version field return expected variant)
Perf profiles published to docs site and linked in Console model page
Automated perf/regression tests pass in CI with defined thresholds
PRs merged and docs patch released with migration notes and example snippets
steps: Create catalog metadata records in catalog-service repo (fields: canonical_id, display_name, versions[], recommended_pinning, runtime_compat, memory_mb_estimate, tokens_per_second_estimate)
Add performance profiles generated from benchmarking harness (90th/50th latency, throughput for batch sizes, GPU memory usage) to docs/perf-profiles directory
Update Console UI to surface 'recommended pin' and perf profile link on model detail page
Add SDK examples and README snippets demonstrating model_version pinning and fallback policy configuration
Add integration tests in inference-endpoint-tests that call both variants and assert latency/throughput and functional sanity on the canonical prompt set
